Maya R: Heads-up — hit a staging OOM during last night's continuous-batcher perf run. Looks like KV cache pressure wasn't consulted when forming batches with a mix of long sequences. Repro: ~20% 4k-chat + 80% 1k-chat. :grimacing:
Alex W: ugh. any logs?
Maya R: pasted the admission trace snippet: ```BATCH_ADMIT: tokens=5600 queue_budget=6000 kv_free_est=1200 kernel_pref=fast_matmul``` then OOM at kv_alloc. The batch was allowed even though kv_free_est < estimated_kv_needed (~2k).
Jin K: that's the admission calc we relaxed last month to favor latency — sounds like we forgot to cap by kv_free_est when sequence variance > 2x. Idea: two-stage check — (1) soft admit for small batches (tokens <= queue_budget/2), (2) strict admit requiring kv_free_est >= estimated_kv_needed for large batches.
Lina P: alternative: compute token_budget = min(queue_budget, floor(kv_free_est / kv_bytes_per_token)). Translate KV bytes to equivalent tokens and gate admission that way. Simpler to reason about.
Sam T: also kernel selection matters. The `fast_matmul` kernel increases peak temporary KV usage for long seqs — prefer `memory_lean` kernel when kv_free_est is low. Tradeoff ~8-12% latency increase but avoids OOM.
perf-bot: perf/profile/2140016000/results.html (summary): 4k-heavy mix shows a ~2.3x memory spike during the matmul step. Flamegraph attached to the job.
Maya R: proposal: admission algorithm -> budget = min(queue_budget, floor(kv_free_est / kv_bytes_per_token)); if budget < kernel_switch_threshold then prefer memory_lean kernel; require strict_kv_check for batches with tokens > large_batch_threshold; add a safety cap at 1.1x estimated_kv_needed. I'll open a PR with the heuristic.
Alex W: include metrics: `admitted_by_soft`, `denied_by_kv`, `kernel_switch_count`, `kv_prefetch_evictions`. Also add a probation window (30s) to avoid oscillation.
Jin K: agree. We'll run a canary on the dedicated pool with a conservative threshold. I'll wire up A/B: 10% new heuristic, 90% baseline.
Lina P: note: kernel switching could cause KV prefetch/evict thrash. Add `kernel_cooldown_ms=5000` and an eviction-debounce so we don't flail.
Sam T: test plan: 1) unit tests for admission math + edge cases, 2) e2e staging with mixed seqs and KV instrumentation, 3) 24h canary on dedicated. Jin + Maya to pair this week; PR by Wed; canary Thu.
Maya R: ack — I'll collect the perf traces and push an initial PR draft. @perf-bot can you run a deeper allocation profile for the 4k path?
perf-bot: queued allocation job for `alloc/profile/4k-path` — ETA ~2h.
Maya R: thanks. I'll add a short script to produce `kv_bytes_per_token` estimates per model and attach to PR.
Alex W: one more ask — add a debug endpoint to force `memory_lean` kernel per-worker so we can repro without changing admission logic.
Jin K: good call. I'll add a `?kernel=memory_lean` flag to the local dev endpoint.
Lina P: small follow-up: update the rollout playbook docs with the metrics and failure-mode runbook (how to roll back to baseline if canary shows perf regressions).
Sam T: cool. If the canary avoids OOMs but latency is up, we can try a middle-ground kernel config or micro-batching to reduce matmul spikes.
Maya R: logging notes for PR: include `kv_free_est`, `estimated_kv_needed`, `kernel_choice`, and `admission_reason` per-batch. Keep logs compact.
perf-bot: allocation job finished — uploaded `alloc/profile/4k-path/2140016000.html`. Summary: large-kernel path has transient +1.9GB scratch alloc.
Alex W: perfect. Thanks everyone — let's sync after the PR lands and check the canary graphs tomorrow. :thumbsup:
